title: Automated Legacy Financial Reconciliation
business: Mid-sized accounting firms managing legacy desktop-based banking software that lacks modern APIs.
problem: Manual data entry from proprietary desktop banking interfaces into cloud-based ERP systems is error-prone and labor-intensive, creating significant operational bottlenecks during month-end closing.
solution: The computer-use-preview model enables the automation of these legacy interfaces by interpreting visual screen data and executing mouse and keyboard inputs directly, effectively bridging the gap between non-API legacy software and modern data workflows.
steps: Configure the environment to host the legacy desktop application in a virtualized, headless display session.
Initialize the computer-use-preview model within the Responses API to process visual snapshots of the banking interface.
Define tool-use functions that map model-generated coordinates and keystrokes to specific UI elements like buttons or input fields.
Implement a control loop that captures screen state, sends it to the model, and executes the returned tool calls to perform reconciliation.
Validate the output by comparing the final screen state against expected ledger balances before committing data to the cloud ERP.
outcome: A reliable, automated pipeline that mimics human interaction with legacy software, reducing manual reconciliation time and minimizing transcription errors.
limitation: The model is constrained by a 1,024 max output token limit per response, which may truncate complex multi-step interaction sequences; developers should check for incomplete tool execution sequences by monitoring the finish_reason in the API response.
